newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bizarre Brazil soap opera murder to go to trial.
newsitem.headline: Bizarre Brazil soap opera murder to go to trial.

text.p: A Brazilian actor and his wife were to go on trial on Wednesday for their role in the brutal murder of a young actress who was the alleged murderer's co-star in a prime time soap opera.

Court officials expected a torrent of media publicity to surround the trial of Guilherme de Padua and his wife, Paula Thomaz, who are accused of stabbing to death 22-year-old actress Daniela Perez in December 1992.
For the last four years, Brazilians have been fascinated by the murder of Perez, who played the sexy Yasmin in the prime time soap "De Corpo e Alma" (Of Body and Soul).
De Padua, who in the show played Yasmin's brooding boyfriend, at first confessed to having murdered Perez after alleging she had pursued him and made repeated demands that he have sex with her.
But he later changed his story to say Perez had in fact been murdered in a fit of jealousy by his wife, Paula Thomaz.
Although he admitted he had been present at the scene of the crime, De Padua said he had been incapable of stopping his half-crazed wife.
Thomaz, who was 19 years old and pregnant at the time, claims Perez was killed by her husband while she was window-shopping at a nearby mall.
Police found Perez's body lying in a wooded area of the luxury beachfront suburb of Barra da Tijuca, her nose and face beaten and disfigured.
They said her body had been stabbed 15 times with a pair of scissors and there were signs her death had been preceded by a violent struggle.
Lawyers for De Padua and Thomaz, who were imprisoned shortly after the murder took place, had managed to postpone the trial for the last four years.
Perez's mother, soap opera screenwriter Gloria Perez, has launched a nationwide campaign in her daughter's memory to protest violence against women.
Thousands of Daniela Perez's fans were expected to mob the Rio de Janeiro courthouse when the trial begins at 1 p.m. local time (1500 GMT) on Wednesday.
Fearing the effect that media attention could have on the trial, the presiding judge has banned TV cameras from the courtroom.
